steps.q: Does it make a great product or service?

views.text: In July 2024, Equity Mates highlighted Nike’s global athlete partnerships and its biggest-ever Olympic marketing push to keep the brand relevant and launch new products like the Alphafly, reinforcing the pull of its footwear and apparel.

episode.title: Is Nike undervalued, the Aussie dollar is rising & investing for kids

views.text: In April 2023, Equity Mates recounted how the Jordan line reshaped Nike, noting the Jordan brand generated about 3 million dollars every five hours, showing powerful consumer demand for its products.

In January 2023, Equity Mates said Nike spent $1.5 billion on athlete endorsements in 2022 and noted strong on-court uptake, with 64% of 442 NBA players wearing Nike shoes, reflecting product desirability.

episode.title: Still a growth company? - Nike | Summer Series

steps.q: Will it keep earning above market profits?

views.text: In July 2024, Equity Mates noted resilience despite negative headlines, with gross margin up, overheads cut 9% in the quarter, EPS up, and 21 consecutive years of dividend growth, indicating an ability to sustain profitability.

episode.title: Is Nike undervalued, the Aussie dollar is rising & investing for kids

views.text: In March 2022, Equity Mates played Nike’s update showing Nike Digital reached 25% of brand revenue, more than double since fiscal 2019, with member-centric initiatives driving growth and strengthening customer relationships.

episode.title: Compair the pair - CEOs go head to head | Quartr Reporting Season

steps.q: Can it reinvest its profits productively?

views.text: In July 2024, Equity Mates reported Nike planned its biggest Olympic marketing spend to reach about a billion viewers while unveiling innovations like the Alphafly, showing management prioritised reinvestment in brand and product.

episode.title: Is Nike undervalued, the Aussie dollar is rising & investing for kids

views.text: In November 2022, Equity Mates relayed a pitch that Nike increased direct-to-consumer from 23% of revenue in 2015 to 43%, invested heavily in technology, and maintained about a 4 billion dollar annual marketing budget to drive growth.

steps.q: Can it be bought at a reasonable price?

views.text: In August 2026, Equity Mates contrasted valuation swings, saying Nike traded near 10 times earnings in 2009, peaked around 70 times during COVID, and had fallen back to roughly 19 to 20 times, showing how changing multiples drove returns.

episode.title: You can’t spend your way out of a population crisis, a robot just beat Usain Bolt & an introduction to factor investing

views.text: In March 2025, a guest on Equity Mates said the market expected Nike to struggle due to inflation, China and a thin product pipeline, and explained it had been added at a small weight with scope to build if conditions improved.

episode.title: Basis Points: Understanding Market Expectations with Matt Wacher of Morningstar
